editorial.headline: Aerial Photography Is Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Aerial photography is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks its PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
KBLI 74201 is about making photographs from the air: images captured with aircraft, unmanned aircraft and comparable aerial means. It follows the production of an image from an aerial viewpoint, whether the platform is manned or remote. The scope is centred on the photographic activity, not merely the fact that something flies. It expressly leaves out air transport undertaken for sightseeing, drawing a useful boundary between selling an aerial image and selling a scenic flight. For registration purposes, the activity is aerial photography itself.

The listed access is broad in scale, running from Mikro and Kecil through Menengah to Besar. That makes the record relevant to a small operator as well as a larger enterprise, provided the activity remains inside that photographic scope. At the national level, PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. This is the straightforward national position: a foreign investor can register this activity under PMA up to the full stated ceiling; it is not a partial-ownership category. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali changes that conclusion rather than softening it. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record expressly identifies PMA registration as blocked. There is no separate Bali foreign-ownership percentage in the record. Instead, the stated OSS risk result at the Besar scale is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah across every scope. Under the province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium, Low and Medium-Low risk classifications are blocked for PMA. The record dates that moratorium to 13 May 2026.

The practical reading must therefore keep the national and Bali positions apart. Nationally, the activity permits 100% foreign ownership and is open across every listed scale. In Bali, however, a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA today because of the applicable risk-class outcome. The Bali block does not redefine the activity: it remains aerial photographic work from aircraft, drones or similar means, while sightseeing air transport stays outside its stated scope. Both the national opening and Bali’s registration block are necessary parts of the same answer.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, aerial photography is nevertheless blocked from PMA registration in Bali today.
